Lesson No. 234: Explanation of Verses 1 to 59

Verses 1 to 8

The surah begins with two letters: Ha. Mim. Both are sworn by, and then the Clear Book (al-Kitab al-Mubin) is also sworn by, which is itself composed of the same letters of the alphabet. We have spoken repeatedly about these letters at the beginning of surahs. Here these letters are sworn by in the same manner as the Clear Book is sworn by. The importance of the Clear Book is accepted, but what is the importance of these letters? The reality is that every letter is itself a miracle and a sign, and every letter is a sign of the structure of human language. Consider also the manner in which the tongue produces that sound from its point of articulation, then the order of the points of articulation of these letters, and then the symbolic indication between the name of each letter and its sound. Through these letters and words, a human being reaches great truths and compiles sciences. This is so great a task that if we reflect upon it seriously and cast aside our habit and familiarity, we will see how great a thing a single letter is. Therefore they have been sworn by.

What is the thing for which this oath is sworn? It is that great event which took place in a blessed night, namely the revelation of the Quran.

"Indaa anzalnahu fi..." to "...munthirin" (44:3), "fiha yufraqu kullu amrin hakim" (44:4), "amran min indina innaa kunna mursilin" (44:5), "rahmatan min..." to "...al-'Alim" (44:6): "We sent it down in a blessed night, for We were indeed warning [mankind]. In it every wise matter is decided by Our command. We were indeed sending a Messenger, as a mercy from your Lord; indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."

The blessed night in which the Quran was revealed is the night in which the revelation of the Quran began, and it is one of the nights of the blessed month of Ramadan, as is explicitly stated:

"Shahru Ramadana alladhi unzila fihi al-Quran" – "The month of Ramadan is that in which the Quran was revealed" (2:185). The Quran was not revealed in its entirety on that night, nor was all of it revealed in Ramadan; but its descent to this earth began in the blessed month of Ramadan and then in that blessed night. For Laylat al-Qadr, or the blessed night, this is sufficient. And Allah knows best!

This night is truly blessed, in which this great door of divine mercy was opened for humanity, and in which the Islamic system of life began to take root in human life, through which a human being became acquainted with the nature of the fitrah. This is most beautifully expressed in the Quran. The human fitrah responds to this system, accepts it gladly, and thus, in accordance with the fitrah, a system is established which is in exact conformity with the demands of human nature and also in exact conformity with the universe in which man lives. This system is established so purely, so naturally and without any hardship, and under its shade a human being lives on the earth, yet in reality he lives in the heavens.

The Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) and the first people upon whom this Quran was revealed lived for a period under that very sky and above that very earth, in a life connected and linked with Allah. Allah would immediately inform them that such and such thoughts had arisen in their hearts, and that He was watching. They were also certain that Allah was watching, and that Allah is our Guardian, aware of every inclination and every whisper of the heart and then every movement of the body. These people would seek refuge first in Him in their affairs, and they were certain that Allah is near, that He hears, and that He answers supplications.

That elect group departed, and after them the Quran remained as an open book, connected with the hearts of human beings. It continued to affect a person in a way that was not possible for any sorcerer. But this effect occurred upon those who, on reading this Quran, opened their hearts. Nevertheless, the hearts and visions of human beings sometimes change in such a way that these transformations sometimes appear like fiction; a person cannot even believe them.

This Quran remained as a system of life. Its system was complete, clear and most pure, granting "humanity." Wherever the Quranic system of life was established, in whatever society it remained, in whatever era it remained, it remained an exemplary system. Wherever the Quranic system of life was established, and in whatever age it was established, under the light of this divine system an outstanding human life came into being, and within it all the characteristics of human life remained. This distinction belongs to the Islamic system of life alone: wherever it is established, there arises a life and a society of such high standard, and it is a society whose establishment involves no human striving, but comes into being through the blessing of this system and through divine power.

The institutions that human beings build can be useful only for human beings like themselves, and can function only within a particular time and place. But the institutions and laws that Allah has made, He has endowed with the quality of permanence. Within them He has placed the utmost beauty and perfection, and He has given them a capacity that transcends the limits of every time and place, in which the real truth remains in its place, and which takes on wonderful forms according to every time and place.

Allah sent down this Quran in that specific night so that people might be warned.

"Inna kunna mundhirin" (44:3): "Indeed We were warning [mankind]." Because Allah knew that this human being is very heedless and in need of warning.

The night in which the Quran was revealed became, because of the revelation of the Quran, a night of decision and of distinguishing between truth and falsehood:

"Fiha yufraqu kullu amrin hakim" (44:4): "In it every wise matter is decided by Our command." In that night, through this Quran, every matter was decided, every dispute was settled. In that night a decision was made between truth and falsehood; falsehood was erased, limits were fixed, and signposts were set for the journey of humanity upon this earth, and these matters were settled until the Day of Resurrection. Accordingly, all the principles upon which individual and collective life in this world is established were fixed, just as for the functioning of this universe Allah has placed all its principles within it.

(The difference between this commentary and the translation of Maulana Maududi, which I have given, is clear. Sayyid Qutb takes "yufraqu" in the sense of "separation/distinction," which does not appear correct. – Translator.)

These decisions were made by the will of Allah, because it was His will, and it has been His practice, that Messengers be sent so that they might expound the Word of Allah and judge in accordance with it.

"Inna kunna mursilin" (44:5): "We were indeed sending a Messenger." The sending of a Messenger was a requirement of Allah's mercy. On the Day of Resurrection, Allah wished to show mercy to the people.

"Rahmatan min rabbika innahu huwa as-Sami' al-'Alim" (44:6): "As a mercy from your Lord; indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." Through the revelation of the Quran, the mercy of Allah manifested in a way that no other mercy has manifested. This Quran settles into hearts with great ease and swiftness, and a person acts in response to it automatically, just as blood flows in the human body. Thus this human being becomes a most serious and noble person, and human society appears like a beautiful dream, and this dream is a practical dream that stands before one's eyes.

This ideology which the Quran presented, in its comprehensiveness and harmony, is so beautiful a belief that a person spontaneously begins to love it; hearts become attached to it. This ideology is not only based upon goodness and righteousness; perfection and comprehensiveness exist within it, and these qualities develop within it to such an extent that they reach the level of compelling beauty. This beauty is so complete and comprehensive that every single part of this belief and system is most beautiful. Moreover, its partial and total beauty and perfection is in harmony with the partial and total beauty and perfection of this universe.

This Quran was sent down as "rahmatan min rabbika" (44:6): "a mercy from your Lord." And it was sent down in this blessed night.

"Innahu huwa as-Sami' al-'Alim" (44:6): "Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." He hears and He knows. The speech and commands that Allah sends down, He sends down on the basis of knowledge and understanding. He knows the words and deeds of people, and He sends down principles and laws that benefit them, through which they are reformed.

He is Allah, the One who guards this universe, its protector and the guardian of all things within it.

"Rabbi as-samawati wal-ardi wa ma baynahuma in kuntum muqinin" (44:7): "The Lord of the heavens and the earth and of whatever is between them, if you are certain." Therefore, the speech and system He sends down for people, He sends for their training, just as His lordship operates in this universe. Man is also part of it, and man is also a part of Allah's laws of nature. The reference here to faith and certainty is because their beliefs were highly unsettled and wavering: on the one hand they regarded the heavens and the earth as the creation of Allah, while on the other hand they had also taken other lords besides Allah. This shows that their conception of Allah was very vague, unclear, superficial and far from firmness. Yet Allah is the one true God, who holds the power of life and death, and is the Lord of the first and the last.

"La ilaha illa huwa yuhyi wa yumit rabbukum wa rabbu aba'ikumu al-awwalin" (44:8): "There is no god but Him. He gives life and He causes death, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers who have passed away." The giving of life and the causing of death are both matters that all human beings see, and they also know that no one except Allah can do these things. This requires only ordinary reflection and contemplation. The sight of death and the story of life both affect the human heart very closely. Through them a person's heart becomes ready to be moved and affected, and then he becomes disposed to accept the truth. For this reason it is mentioned frequently in the Quran, and the human heart and mind are repeatedly directed toward it, and the hearts of the believers are repeatedly washed by it.

"Fiha yufraqu kullu amrin hakim" (44:4): "In it every wise matter is decided by Our command." In that night, through this Quran, every matter was decided, every dispute was settled. "Inna kunna mursilin" (44:5): "We were indeed sending a Messenger." The sending of a Messenger was a requirement of Allah's mercy. On the Day of Resurrection, Allah wished to show mercy to the people.

"Rahmatan min rabbika innahu huwa as-Sami' al-'Alim" (44:6): "As a mercy from your Lord; indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." Through the revelation of the Quran, the mercy of Allah manifested in a way that no other mercy has manifested. This Quran settles into hearts with great ease and swiftness, and a person acts in response to it automatically, just as blood flows in the human body. Thus this human being becomes a most serious and noble person, and human society appears like a beautiful dream, and this dream is a practical dream that stands before one's eyes.

This ideology which the Quran presented, in its comprehensiveness and harmony, is so beautiful a belief that a person spontaneously begins to love it; hearts become attached to it. This ideology is not only based upon goodness and righteousness; perfection and comprehensiveness exist within it, and these qualities develop within it to such an extent that they reach the level of compelling beauty. This beauty is so complete and comprehensive that every single part of this belief and system is most beautiful. Moreover, its partial and total beauty and perfection is in harmony with the partial and total beauty and perfection of this universe.

This Quran was sent down as "rahmatan min rabbika" (44:6): "a mercy from your Lord." And it was sent down in this blessed night.

"Innahu huwa as-Sami' al-'Alim" (44:6): "Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." He hears and He knows. The speech and commands that Allah sends down, He sends down on the basis of knowledge and understanding. He knows the words and deeds of people, and He sends down principles and laws that benefit them, through which they are reformed.

He is Allah, the One who guards this universe, its protector and the guardian of all things within it.

The reference here to faith and certainty is because their beliefs were highly unsettled and wavering: on the one hand they regarded the heavens and the earth as the creation of Allah, while on the other hand they had also taken other lords besides Allah. This shows that their conception of Allah was very vague, unclear, superficial and far from firmness. Yet Allah is the one true God, who holds the power of life and death, and is the Lord of the first and the last.

"La ilaha illa huwa yuhyi wa yumit rabbukum wa rabbu aba'ikumu al-awwalin" (44:8): "There is no god but Him. He gives life and He causes death, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers who have passed away." The giving of life and the causing of death are both matters that all human beings see, and they also know that no one except Allah can do these things. This requires only ordinary reflection and contemplation. The sight of death and the story of life both affect the human heart very closely. Through them a person's heart becomes ready to be moved and affected, and then he becomes disposed to accept the truth. For this reason it is mentioned frequently in the Quran, and the human heart and mind are repeatedly directed toward it, and the hearts of the believers are repeatedly washed by it.

Lesson No. 234: Explanation of Verses 1 to 59

Verses 1 to 8

The surah begins with two letters: Ha. Mim. Both are sworn by, and then the Clear Book (al-Kitab al-Mubin) is also sworn by, which is itself composed of the same letters of the alphabet. We have spoken repeatedly about these letters at the beginning of surahs. Here these letters are sworn by in the same manner as the Clear Book is sworn by. The importance of the Clear Book is accepted, but what is the importance of these letters? The reality is that every letter is itself a miracle and a sign, and every letter is a sign of the structure of human language. Consider also the manner in which the tongue produces that sound from its point of articulation, then the order of the points of articulation of these letters, and then the symbolic indication between the name of each letter and its sound. Through these letters and words, a human being reaches great truths and compiles sciences. This is so great a task that if we reflect upon it seriously and cast aside our habit and familiarity, we will see how great a thing a single letter is. Therefore they have been sworn by.

What is the thing for which this oath is sworn? It is that great event which took place in a blessed night, namely the revelation of the Quran.

"Indaa anzalnahu fi..." to "...munthirin" (44:3), "fiha yufraqu kullu amrin hakim" (44:4), "amran min indina innaa kunna mursilin" (44:5), "rahmatan min..." to "...al-'Alim" (44:6): "We sent it down in a blessed night, for We were indeed warning [mankind]. The blessed night in which the Quran was revealed is the night in which the revelation of the Quran began, and it is one of the nights of the blessed month of Ramadan, as is explicitly stated:

"Shahru Ramadana alladhi unzila fihi al-Quran" – "The month of Ramadan is that in which the Quran was revealed" (2:185). Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 44, verses 9–16 (part 1 of 2):

After having so impressed, stirred and moved the addressees of the Qur'an towards accepting the truth, the direction of speech now suddenly turns, and the other side of the picture is presented: what is the condition of these people after this great Book's effort? The truth is that the picture drawn here of these people should not be the case. Yet these people are so hard-hearted that, despite such earnest efforts, they still consider this movement to be merely a joke.

Verses 9 to 16.

It is said that they adopt a frivolous attitude towards this so wise and magnificent doctrine and system, and they doubt the signs which are established. Therefore, the correct remedy for them is to leave them to that day which will be very severe and nerve-shattering.

﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke, which will envelop the people. This is a painful punishment.﴾ "Our Lord, remove the punishment from us; we are indeed believers."

Among the righteous predecessors (salaf al-salihin) there has been difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of the verse of smoke (ayat al-dukhan). Some said that it is the smoke of the Day of Resurrection; the threat stated here, that you wait for it, is like that found in other places in the Qur'an where waiting for the punishment of the Resurrection is mentioned, and it is indeed going to come. People also wait, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also waited. But some people held the view that this event has actually already passed: just as the Qur'an gave the threat, and then when it came, the polytheists came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he made supplication, and this punishment was removed. Here we quote both opinions and their chains of transmission, and after that we will give our own commentary.

Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash narrated from Abu al-Duha Muslim ibn Subaih, from Masruq, who says: I entered a mosque in Kufa with Abwab al-Kinda, where a man was explaining to his companions:

﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke.﴾ "Do you people know what this smoke is? It is a smoke which will come on the Day of Resurrection. By it the hypocrites and disbelievers will become blind and deaf, and the believers will be affected only to the extent that a cold affects a person." He said: We came to Ibn Mas'ud (ra) and mentioned this matter to him. At that time he was reclining on a pillow; he sat up in agitation, and said: Allah said to your Prophet (ﷺ):

﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, and I am not of those who burden themselves.﴾ "This too is a proof of great knowledge: that if someone does not know a matter, he should say, 'Allah knows best.' Regarding this, I tell you the actual matter. When the Quraysh did not accept Islam in any form, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) supplicated: O Allah, send upon them years like those which came in the time of Yusuf (peace be upon him) in Egypt. So hardship, hunger and thirst came upon them, until they began to eat bones, and also ate carrion. Conditions became such that they would raise their eyes to the sky and see only smoke, and in some narrations the words are that a man would raise his gaze towards another and the atmosphere would appear as though it were smoke, and this was due to their wretched state. Regarding this Allah said:

﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke. It will envelop the people. This is a painful punishment.﴾ People came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and it was said to him: Ask the Messenger of Allah to pray for the Mudar tribe of Arabs, for they are about to perish. The Prophet (ﷺ) prayed for them for the rain of mercy, and rain came. Upon this these verses were revealed:

﴿We will remove the punishment a little; indeed you will return [to your previous ways].﴾ "We are removing the punishment a little; you will again do what you were doing before." Ibn Mas'ud (ra) further said: Could it be that on the Day of Resurrection the punishment would be lifted from them? Thus, when they again attained prosperity, they returned to their old ways. So Allah revealed this verse:

﴿The day We shall seize with the greatest seizing; indeed We will take retribution.﴾ "The day when We will strike with a great blow is the day when We will take vengeance upon you." Its meaning is the Day of Badr. Ibn Mas'ud (ra) said that five things have passed: the smoke, the Rum, the splitting of the moon, the great seizing, and the lizam. This hadith is narrated in the Sahihayn. Imam Ahmad has also related it. Tirmidhi and Nasa'i have also given it in Kitab al-Tafsir. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim have related it from al-A'mash through several routes. In the interpretation of this verse, a group has agreed with Ibn Mas'ud (ra) that the event of the smoke has passed, such as Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak and 'Ata' al-'Awfi, and this same interpretation has been adopted by Ibn Jarir.

But the opinion of other people is that the event of the smoke has not passed; rather it is among the signs of the Hour which are yet to come. We were discussing the Hour when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not be established until ten signs have appeared: (1) the rising of the sun from the west, (2) the smoke, (3) the beast (dabbah), (4) the emergence of Gog and Magog, (5) the emergence of Jesus son of Mary, (6) the Dajjal, (7) three eclipses, (8) the sinking of the earth in the east, (9) the sinking of the earth in the west, (10) the sinking of the earth in the Arabian Peninsula. And a fire will emerge from the depths of Aden; it will drive the people or gather the people; wherever they spend the night, it will be there, and wherever they rest during the day, it too will rest." (Muslim)

Allama Ibn Jarir has narrated: from Muhammad ibn 'Awf, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, from his father, from Dhaighum ibn Zar'ah, from Surayj ibn 'Ubayd, and from Hadrat Malik al-Ash'ari (ra), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Indeed your Lord has warned you of three things: the smoke which will affect the believer like a cold, and for the disbeliever its effect will be that he will swell up, and it will come out of every opening of his body; the second is the Beast of the Earth; and the third is the Dajjal. This hadith has been narrated by al-Tabarani from Hashim ibn Yazid, and he from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash with the same text (Ibn Kathir said: this chain is jayyid).

Ibn Jarir has narrated, from Ya'qub, from Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: One morning I went to Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas (ra), and he said: I did not sleep at all last night until morning. I asked: Why? He said: Today a comet appeared, and it struck me with fear that perhaps the time of the smoke had come, and since then I have not slept until morning. Ibn Abi Hatim has similarly narrated from his father, from Ibn 'Umar, from Sufyan, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Yazid, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah, and from Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas (ra).

Allama Ibn Kathir says: This chain is sahih up to Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas, who is a great scholar of this ummah and the interpreter of the Qur'an. And this view has been adopted by Companions and Successors who agreed with him. And in this regard he has presented several marfu' and hasan hadiths, which fully satisfy that this smoke mentioned here is among the signs that are awaited, and the apparent meaning of the Qur'an also indicates this. Allah said:

﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke.﴾ That is, the smoke will be perfectly clear, and every person will be able to see it. And from what Ibn Mas'ud has narrated, it appears that it was a matter of imagination, and people were seeing smoke because of hunger and hardship. Then: ﴿It will envelop the people.﴾ That is, it will cover them and blind them. If this were merely an imagined matter, felt only by the people of Makkah, then the expression "it will envelop the people" would not have been used. Then comes:

﴿This is a painful punishment.﴾ That is, it will be said to them, as a rebuke and reproach, as in another place:

﴿The Day they will be pushed into the fire of Hell with a violent push: "This is the Fire which you used to deny."﴾

It is possible that they will say to one another that this is a painful punishment, and after that the verse:

﴿Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed we are believers.﴾ That is, the disbelievers will say when they have seen that the punishment of Allah has come and that this is indeed a retribution, they will ask: O Lord, remove this punishment, as Allah said in another place:

﴿And if you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire, they will say: "Would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers."﴾ And in the same way, this verse has the same theme.

﴿And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come upon them. Then the wrongdoers will say: "Our Lord, grant us a little respite; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers." Were you not those who swore before that there would be no decline for you?﴾ In the verse following the one under discussion, Allah says:

﴿Yet how would they have the reminder, when there had come to them a clear Messenger? Then they turned away from him and said, "A taught, mad one."﴾ That is, how can they benefit from admonition? We sent to them a Messenger who clearly presented the call before them, warned them, yet they turned away, did not accept anything he said, rather denied him and said that he is a taught madman.

A similar example is in the Qur'an also:

﴿On that Day man will remember, but how will remembrance benefit him?﴾ And in another verse similarly:

﴿If you could see when they will be terrified and cannot escape, and will be seized from a near place. Then they will say, "We believed in it," but how can attainment come from a far place?﴾ After the above-mentioned verse 14, this verse comes:

﴿We will remove the punishment a little; indeed you will return [to your ways].﴾ "We are about to remove the punishment a little, but you will again do what you were doing before." This verse can have two meanings: one is that if We remove the punishment and return you to the world, you will again do what you did before, i.e., disbelief and denial; and examples of this are found in other verses too:

﴿And if We had mercy upon them and removed what afflicts them, they would persist in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ And as in another verse:

﴿And if they were returned, they would certainly return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾ The second meaning may be: We are actually holding back the punishment from you, or are about to hold it back, while you keep increasing in insolence and misguidance; because for the removal of punishment it is not necessary that the punishment has actually come upon them. Elsewhere Allah said:

﴿Except the people of Yunus; when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and granted them enjoyment for a period.﴾ Although the punishment had not actually touched them, but the causes of punishment had been gathered. Qatadah has taken the meaning that you are about to return to the punishment of Allah. The next verse is:

﴿The Day We will seize with the greatest seizure; indeed We will take retribution.﴾ Hadrat Ibn Mas'ud (ra) interpreted it as the Battle of Badr, and some others who agreed with Ibn Mas'ud have also adopted this view, and the same interpretation is related from Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas as well. This has been narrated from him by 'Awfi, and this is also the opinion of Hadrat Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and it is also a possibility, but the apparent meaning is that this too refers to the Day of Resurrection, although the Day of Badr was also a day of great seizure for the disbelievers. Ibn Jarir has narrated from Ya'qub, from Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Khalid al-Hadha', from 'Ikrimah, who said that Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas (ra) said: "Ibn Mas'ud (ra) says that the great seizure refers to the day of Badr. My view is that it is the Day of Resurrection." The chain of this hadith is sahih. Hasan al-Basri and 'Ikrimah, according to a sahih narration, also hold this view. Here ends the speech of Ibn Kathir.

We adopt here the view of Ibn Abbas that the smoke (al-dukhan) will occur on the Day of Resurrection, and Allamah Ibn Kathir has explained it very well. It is a threat and a warning to the disbelievers, and there are many parallels to it in the Quran, in which the same meaning is repeated in other places. In this way the meaning would be: these people are in doubt and are occupied with play and amusement; leave them, and wait for that day, the frightening day, when a smoke will come from the sky, will cover all people, and it will be said: this is a painful punishment. Then the scene of their supplication is depicted: "O our Lord, remove this punishment from us; we believe." And their request is rejected, since its granting is impossible, because the time has passed. "Now how can they receive admonition? A clear Messenger had come to them, yet they turned away from him and said: he is a taught madman. A foreign slave is teaching him these things." And this is false.

In this scene, where these people request the lifting of the punishment, a parenthetical remark is addressed to them: Look, you are still in the world. Brief moments of respite remain, you are still spared from the punishment, so believe. You are being warned that it is you who will be eager to believe in the Hereafter, but faith will not be accepted there. You are still in peace and well-being, and this peace and well-being is not permanent. You are going to be brought before Us (a'idun).

"On the day when We will seize them with the greatest seizing" (44:16), which is the day of this smoke that the Quran depicts, there will be seizing and punishment; then "We will indeed take vengeance" (44:16). This is for your carelessness, and for your slander, which you direct at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "a taught, mad one" (44:14), although he is truthful and trustworthy.

In this way the interpretation of all the verses becomes correct, according to our understanding. And Allah knows best!

٭٭٭٭

After this, the Quran takes them into a valley of history. This is a brief portion of the story of Musa (peace be upon him), and its conclusion is an example of that great seizing (al-batshah al-kubra, 44:16), on this earth, of which an example had already been shown to them in the depiction of the smoke.

This hadith is narrated in the Sahihayn. Imam Ahmad has also related it. Tirmidhi and Nasa'i have also given it in Kitab al-Tafsir. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim have related it from al-A'mash through several routes. In the interpretation of this verse, a group has agreed with Ibn Mas'ud (ra) that the event of the smoke has passed, such as Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak and 'Ata' al-'Awfi, and this same interpretation has been adopted by Ibn Jarir.

But the opinion of other people is that the event of the smoke has not passed; rather it is among the signs of the Hour which are yet to come. We were discussing the Hour when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not be established until ten signs have appeared: (1) the rising of the sun from the west, (2) the smoke, (3) the beast (dabbah), (4) the emergence of Gog and Magog, (5) the emergence of Jesus son of Mary, (6) the Dajjal, (7) three eclipses, (8) the sinking of the earth in the east, (9) the sinking of the earth in the west, (10) the sinking of the earth in the Arabian Peninsula. And a fire will emerge from the depths of Aden; it will drive the people or gather the people; wherever they spend the night, it will be there, and wherever they rest during the day, it too will rest." (Muslim)

Allama Ibn Jarir has narrated: from Muhammad ibn 'Awf, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, from his father, from Dhaighum ibn Zar'ah, from Surayj ibn 'Ubayd, and from Hadrat Malik al-Ash'ari (ra), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Indeed your Lord has warned you of three things: the smoke which will affect the believer like a cold, and for the disbeliever its effect will be that he will swell up, and it will come out of every opening of his body; the second is the Beast of the Earth; and the third is the Dajjal. This hadith has been narrated by al-Tabarani from Hashim ibn Yazid, and he from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash with the same text (Ibn Kathir said: this chain is jayyid).

Ibn Jarir has narrated, from Ya'qub, from Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: One morning I went to Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas (ra), and he said: I did not sleep at all last night until morning. I asked: Why? He said: Today a comet appeared, and it struck me with fear that perhaps the time of the smoke had come, and since then I have not slept until morning. Ibn Abi Hatim has similarly narrated from his father, from Ibn 'Umar, from Sufyan, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Yazid, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah, and from Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas (ra).

Allama Ibn Kathir says: This chain is sahih up to Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas, who is a great scholar of this ummah and the interpreter of the Qur'an. And this view has been adopted by Companions and Successors who agreed with him. And in this regard he has presented several marfu' and hasan hadiths, which fully satisfy that this smoke mentioned here is among the signs that are awaited, and the apparent meaning of the Qur'an also indicates this. Allah said:

﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke.﴾ That is, the smoke will be perfectly clear, and every person will be able to see it. And from what Ibn Mas'ud has narrated, it appears that it was a matter of imagination, and people were seeing smoke because of hunger and hardship. Then: ﴿It will envelop the people.﴾ That is, it will cover them and blind them. If this were merely an imagined matter, felt only by the people of Makkah, then the expression "it will envelop the people" would not have been used. Then comes:

﴿This is a painful punishment.﴾ That is, it will be said to them, as a rebuke and reproach, as in another place:

﴿The Day they will be pushed into the fire of Hell with a violent push: "This is the Fire which you used to deny."﴾

It is possible that they will say to one another that this is a painful punishment, and after that the verse:

﴿Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed we are believers.﴾ That is, the disbelievers will say when they have seen that the punishment of Allah has come and that this is indeed a retribution, they will ask: O Lord, remove this punishment, as Allah said in another place:

﴿And if you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire, they will say: "Would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers."﴾ And in the same way, this verse has the same theme.

﴿And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come upon them. Then the wrongdoers will say: "Our Lord, grant us a little respite; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers." Were you not those who swore before that there would be no decline for you?﴾ In the verse following the one under discussion, Allah says:

﴿Yet how would they have the reminder, when there had come to them a clear Messenger? Then they turned away from him and said, "A taught, mad one."﴾ That is, how can they benefit from admonition? We sent to them a Messenger who clearly presented the call before them, warned them, yet they turned away, did not accept anything he said, rather denied him and said that he is a taught madman.

A similar example is in the Qur'an also:

﴿On that Day man will remember, but how will remembrance benefit him?﴾ And in another verse similarly:

﴿If you could see when they will be terrified and cannot escape, and will be seized from a near place. Then they will say, "We believed in it," but how can attainment come from a far place?﴾ After the above-mentioned verse 14, this verse comes:

﴿We will remove the punishment a little; indeed you will return [to your ways].﴾ "We are about to remove the punishment a little, but you will again do what you were doing before." This verse can have two meanings: one is that if We remove the punishment and return you to the world, you will again do what you did before, i.e., disbelief and denial; and examples of this are found in other verses too:

﴿And if We had mercy upon them and removed what afflicts them, they would persist in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ And as in another verse:

﴿And if they were returned, they would certainly return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾ The second meaning may be: We are actually holding back the punishment from you, or are about to hold it back, while you keep increasing in insolence and misguidance; because for the removal of punishment it is not necessary that the punishment has actually come upon them. Elsewhere Allah said:

﴿Except the people of Yunus; when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and granted them enjoyment for a period.﴾ Although the punishment had not actually touched them, but the causes of punishment had been gathered. Qatadah has taken the meaning that you are about to return to the punishment of Allah. The next verse is:

﴿The Day We will seize with the greatest seizure; indeed We will take retribution.﴾ Hadrat Ibn Mas'ud (ra) interpreted it as the Battle of Badr, and some others who agreed with Ibn Mas'ud have also adopted this view, and the same interpretation is related from Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas as well. This has been narrated from him by 'Awfi, and this is also the opinion of Hadrat Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and it is also a possibility, but the apparent meaning is that this too refers to the Day of Resurrection, although the Day of Badr was also a day of great seizure for the disbelievers. Ibn Jarir has narrated from Ya'qub, from Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Khalid al-Hadha', from 'Ikrimah, who said that Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas (ra) said: "Ibn Mas'ud (ra) says that the great seizure refers to the day of Badr. My view is that it is the Day of Resurrection." The chain of this hadith is sahih. Hasan al-Basri and 'Ikrimah, according to a sahih narration, also hold this view. Here ends the speech of Ibn Kathir.

We adopt here the view of Ibn Abbas that the smoke (al-dukhan) will occur on the Day of Resurrection, and Allamah Ibn Kathir has explained it very well. It is a threat and a warning to the disbelievers, and there are many parallels to it in the Quran, in which the same meaning is repeated in other places. In this way the meaning would be: these people are in doubt and are occupied with play and amusement; leave them, and wait for that day, the frightening day, when a smoke will come from the sky, will cover all people, and it will be said: this is a painful punishment. Then the scene of their supplication is depicted: "O our Lord, remove this punishment from us; we believe." And their request is rejected, since its granting is impossible, because the time has passed. "Now how can they receive admonition? A clear Messenger had come to them, yet they turned away from him and said: he is a taught madman. A foreign slave is teaching him these things." And this is false.

In this scene, where these people request the lifting of the punishment, a parenthetical remark is addressed to them: Look, you are still in the world. Brief moments of respite remain, you are still spared from the punishment, so believe. You are being warned that it is you who will be eager to believe in the Hereafter, but faith will not be accepted there. You are still in peace and well-being, and this peace and well-being is not permanent. You are going to be brought before Us (a'idun).

"On the day when We will seize them with the greatest seizing" (44:16), which is the day of this smoke that the Quran depicts, there will be seizing and punishment; then "We will indeed take vengeance" (44:16). This is for your carelessness, and for your slander, which you direct at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "a taught, mad one" (44:14), although he is truthful and trustworthy.

In this way the interpretation of all the verses becomes correct, according to our understanding. And Allah knows best!

٭٭٭٭

After this, the Quran takes them into a valley of history. This is a brief portion of the story of Musa (peace be upon him), and its conclusion is an example of that great seizing (al-batshah al-kubra, 44:16), on this earth, of which an example had already been shown to them in the depiction of the smoke.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 44, verses 17–33:**

Verses 17 to 33

At the very door of this valley there is written a frightening proclamation: remember that the sending of a Messenger to a people is a test for them. The deniers should keep in mind that the time is very short. In it you may deny, you may be arrogant and proud, you may give the Messenger pain, you may inflict oppression and cruelty upon the believers. But in the end the head of arrogance is bowed low, and you who provoke the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who fill his cup of patience to overflowing, yet he (ﷺ) remains steadfast in patience, a picture of forbearance, and hopes only for your guidance. The outcome may be bad for you, and you may fall into a severe grip like that of Pharaoh.

﴿And We had already tested before them the people of Pharaoh﴾ (44:17): We had already tested them with blessings, with kingship, and with great power in the land. They were given a long respite amid prosperity, the means of wealth and high standing.

﴿And there came to them a noble Messenger﴾ (44:17): This too was a part of the test. It also shows what the noble Messenger asked them to accept. He did not ask them for anything for himself. He called them to Allah, and his demand was that they should render everything to Allah, and not withhold anything from Allah for their own sake.

﴿Hand over to me the servants of Allah; indeed I am to you a trustworthy Messenger. And do not exalt yourselves against Allah; indeed I bring you a clear authority. And indeed I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me. And if you do not believe me, then keep away from me﴾ (44:18–21): That is, "O servants of Allah, submit everything to me," or "hand over the servants of Allah to me; I am a trustworthy Messenger for you. Do not rebel against Allah. I present before you a clear proof of my commission, and I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from your attacking me. If you do not accept my word, then at least refrain from laying hands on me." This is the brief call that the noble Messenger, namely Moses (peace be upon him), brought. The meaning is that you should completely surrender to Allah before whom you are servants, and give everything to Allah. It does not befit servants to rebel against Allah. This is the call of Allah, and a noble Messenger has come to you with it, and he has a credential of his prophethood. It is a strong and powerful argument. If one reflects with an open heart, one should be convinced by such proofs. He sought refuge in Allah against their violence, lest they seize him and stone him. If they reject faith and separate from the Messenger, he offers them the proposal that he too will separate from them. And this is a most just statement: if you do not accept my word, then do not block my path.

Another interpretation of this verse has also been given:

﴿Hand over to me the servants of Allah﴾ (44:18), that is, hand over the Children of Israel to me and do not subject them to oppression and cruelty. Elsewhere the explicit statement comes: ﴿Send with us the Children of Israel﴾, that is, send the Children of Israel with us. But rebellious people have never accepted the reasonable and just demands of anyone. Rebels do not like to see the truth free, reaching the common people with ease. Therefore every rebel likes to grasp the truth in his own hand and never makes peace with it. For if there is reconciliation between rebels and truth, then truth begins to prevail and keeps conquering the hearts and minds of the masses. This is why falsehood lays hands on truth, stones the people of truth, and does not even let truth remain apart so that it may be safe and at rest.

In the context here, several links of the story have been condensed and presented briefly, so that the reader may be brought quickly to the end, when the trial has reached its limit and Moses (peace be upon him) perceives that these people are by no means going to accept the call, nor are they prepared to let us do our work by tolerating us. And he comes to know that their criminal mentality is very deep and firm, that there is no hope of their reform, and that they will not abandon this mentality. At this point he makes his final appeal to his Lord and seeks complete refuge in Him.

﴿So he called upon his Lord: "These are a people who are criminals"﴾ (44:22): What else can a Messenger do but present the full harvest of his struggle before the court of his Lord, place it before Allah, and leave the next step to Allah? Allah accepted the comment and report that Moses (peace be upon him) had made about his people: that it is true these people are indeed criminals.

﴿So travel by night with My servants; indeed you will be pursued. And leave the sea as it is; indeed they are an army to be drowned﴾ (44:23–24): "Go, then, with My servants by night; you will be pursued. Leave the sea in its state; this whole host is destined to drown." Al-sirr (إِسْرَ) refers to a journey undertaken at night. After this, the word "laylan" (لَيْلًا, "by night") brings the scene back to mind, that some servants of Allah, the Children of Israel, are travelling at night. This word also points to an atmosphere of secrecy, because their night journey was in fact secret from Pharaoh and undertaken without the knowledge of the government. "Al-rahw" (الرَّهْوَ) means calm or stillness. Here Allah commanded Moses (peace be upon him) that he and his people should pass over, and leave the sea behind in a state of calm, in the very state in which he had crossed it, so that Pharaoh and his army would be deceived and follow you, and thus the command of Allah would be fulfilled. ﴿Indeed they are an army to be drowned﴾ (44:24): Thus the decree of Allah was fulfilled according to apparent means, and these means too are in reality a part of Allah's decree.

In the context here, the events of Pharaoh's drowning have been left in summary, because the decision has been stated as: this is an army to be drowned. Now, leaving that scene aside, a comment is made on it, and this comment is itself a striking scene, a narrative of the humiliation of the rebellious and arrogant Pharaoh and his chiefs. It was these very people who kept him inclined toward oppression and rebellion. Their destruction was how easy a matter for Allah. Pharaoh was proud of his position, and his followers were devoted to him. Yet all these people were so small and so insignificant that the universe took no notice of their drowning. Everything was taken from Pharaoh, and there was no one to weep. No one wrote an obituary for his ruin, neither the earth nor the sky.

﴿How many gardens and springs did they leave behind, and fields and noble dwellings, and comforts in which they had delighted? Thus it was, and We made other people inherit them. And the heaven and the earth did not weep for them, nor were they given respite﴾ (44:25–29): The scene here shows the blessings in which they used to revel: gardens, springs, various kinds of crops, great palaces where they enjoyed great honour. They ate, drank, and reveled in these blessings, joyful and intoxicated.

After this, all of it is taken from them, and other peoples are made their heirs. Elsewhere it is said:

﴿Thus, and We made the Children of Israel inherit them﴾: The Children of Israel did not become heirs to Pharaoh's kingdom, yet in Palestine they attained great eminence. The meaning is that they were made heirs to the same kind of blessings as those that had been taken from the Pharaohs.

Then what happened? Pharaoh and his chiefs were annihilated. There was a time when he was the apple of the eye of people on this earth, and his awe was immense in people's hearts; now there is a time when no eye wept at their annihilation. Neither the sky took notice nor the earth, nor were they granted respite, and their affair was set aside.

﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them, nor were they given respite﴾ (44:29): This is a form of expression that shows their abjectness, the faithlessness of the world, and its turning away of its eyes. These rebellious and arrogant people departed from this world, and no eye in earth or heaven wept for them, nor did anything show grief; they passed away as one tramples ants underfoot. Yet they had been so tyrannical and dominating that they used to trample human beings like ants. Why did this happen? Because they were cut off from this universe. The whole universe was Muslim, and they were disbelievers; they were wicked, cast out, and evil people, and the whole universe hated them. If the dictators of this world understood what is in these verses and adopted the guidance they contain, they would know how light they are in this universe and how light they are before Allah. They would realise that they live on this earth utterly alone, cast out, and cut off from the whole universe and from the Creator of the universe. And why? Because they are cut off from bonds of faith and are criminals.

And in contrast to their evil days, the honour and dignity of the believers:

﴿And We certainly delivered the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment, from Pharaoh, who was indeed a haughty one among the transgressors. And We chose them knowingly above the nations, and gave them of the signs that contained a clear trial﴾ (44:30–33).

Here the deliverance of the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment is mentioned, whereas those tyrants who inflicted that torment were annihilated: those who were arrogant and proud and considered themselves great.

﴿From Pharaoh; indeed he was a haughty one among the transgressors﴾ (44:31).

After this, mention is made that Allah preferred the Children of Israel over other peoples, and gave it knowingly. Their good was in Our sight, and their evil was in Our sight too. Therefore in their age We raised them above all nations, because Allah knew that among the peoples of their time they were the most excellent, superior, and outstanding. This shows that Allah Most High sometimes bestows His help and support upon a people who are superior to their contemporaries, even though they may not have reached a high standard of faith and certainty, provided their leadership is good and they are being led upward toward elevation with guidance, knowledge, insight, and steadfastness.

﴿And We gave them of the signs that contained a clear trial﴾ (44:33): Thus they were tested through these signs. When their examination and trial were complete, and the period of their caliphate and their preference over the nations of the world came to an end, then, because of their deviation and error, they were seized, other peoples were set over them, and they were repeatedly faced with exile, and abasement was decreed for them. It was said to them that whenever you exceed the limits and act with rebellion, you will be humiliated and disgraced. This condition will remain until the Day of Resurrection.

***

After the observations of the destructive journey of Pharaoh and his chiefs, in which Moses (peace be upon him) and his people were granted deliverance and they were tested through it, the discourse now turns again to the polytheists' belief in resurrection after death. These people doubted, and indeed denied, being raised after death. This subject is taken up again from the angle that being raised after death is part of the true blueprint of this universe, because it is the truth, the universe itself exists upon the truth, and the demand of truth is that people be raised after death.

And leave the sea as it is; indeed they are an army to be drowned﴾ (44:23–24): "Go, then, with My servants by night; you will be pursued. Leave the sea in its state; this whole host is destined to drown." Al-sirr (إِسْرَ) refers to a journey undertaken at night. After this, the word "laylan" (لَيْلًا, "by night") brings the scene back to mind, that some servants of Allah, the Children of Israel, are travelling at night. This word also points to an atmosphere of secrecy, because their night journey was in fact secret from Pharaoh and undertaken without the knowledge of the government. "Al-rahw" (الرَّهْوَ) means calm or stillness. Here Allah commanded Moses (peace be upon him) that he and his people should pass over, and leave the sea behind in a state of calm, in the very state in which he had crossed it, so that Pharaoh and his army would be deceived and follow you, and thus the command of Allah would be fulfilled. ﴿Indeed they are an army to be drowned﴾ (44:24): Thus the decree of Allah was fulfilled according to apparent means, and these means too are in reality a part of Allah's decree.

In the context here, the events of Pharaoh's drowning have been left in summary, because the decision has been stated as: this is an army to be drowned. Now, leaving that scene aside, a comment is made on it, and this comment is itself a striking scene, a narrative of the humiliation of the rebellious and arrogant Pharaoh and his chiefs. It was these very people who kept him inclined toward oppression and rebellion. Their destruction was how easy a matter for Allah. Pharaoh was proud of his position, and his followers were devoted to him. Yet all these people were so small and so insignificant that the universe took no notice of their drowning. Everything was taken from Pharaoh, and there was no one to weep. No one wrote an obituary for his ruin, neither the earth nor the sky.

﴿How many gardens and springs did they leave behind, and fields and noble dwellings, and comforts in which they had delighted? Thus it was, and We made other people inherit them. And the heaven and the earth did not weep for them, nor were they given respite﴾ (44:25–29): The scene here shows the blessings in which they used to revel: gardens, springs, various kinds of crops, great palaces where they enjoyed great honour. They ate, drank, and reveled in these blessings, joyful and intoxicated.

After this, all of it is taken from them, and other peoples are made their heirs. Elsewhere it is said:

﴿Thus, and We made the Children of Israel inherit them﴾: The Children of Israel did not become heirs to Pharaoh's kingdom, yet in Palestine they attained great eminence. The meaning is that they were made heirs to the same kind of blessings as those that had been taken from the Pharaohs.

Then what happened? Pharaoh and his chiefs were annihilated. There was a time when he was the apple of the eye of people on this earth, and his awe was immense in people's hearts; now there is a time when no eye wept at their annihilation. Neither the sky took notice nor the earth, nor were they granted respite, and their affair was set aside.

﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them, nor were they given respite﴾ (44:29): This is a form of expression that shows their abjectness, the faithlessness of the world, and its turning away of its eyes. These rebellious and arrogant people departed from this world, and no eye in earth or heaven wept for them, nor did anything show grief; they passed away as one tramples ants underfoot. Yet they had been so tyrannical and dominating that they used to trample human beings like ants. Why did this happen? Because they were cut off from this universe. The whole universe was Muslim, and they were disbelievers; they were wicked, cast out, and evil people, and the whole universe hated them. If the dictators of this world understood what is in these verses and adopted the guidance they contain, they would know how light they are in this universe and how light they are before Allah. They would realise that they live on this earth utterly alone, cast out, and cut off from the whole universe and from the Creator of the universe. And why? Because they are cut off from bonds of faith and are criminals.

And in contrast to their evil days, the honour and dignity of the believers:

﴿And We certainly delivered the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment, from Pharaoh, who was indeed a haughty one among the transgressors. And We chose them knowingly above the nations, and gave them of the signs that contained a clear trial﴾ (44:30–33).

Here the deliverance of the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment is mentioned, whereas those tyrants who inflicted that torment were annihilated: those who were arrogant and proud and considered themselves great.

﴿From Pharaoh; indeed he was a haughty one among the transgressors﴾ (44:31).

After this, mention is made that Allah preferred the Children of Israel over other peoples, and gave it knowingly. Their good was in Our sight, and their evil was in Our sight too. Therefore in their age We raised them above all nations, because Allah knew that among the peoples of their time they were the most excellent, superior, and outstanding. This shows that Allah Most High sometimes bestows His help and support upon a people who are superior to their contemporaries, even though they may not have reached a high standard of faith and certainty, provided their leadership is good and they are being led upward toward elevation with guidance, knowledge, insight, and steadfastness.

﴿And We gave them of the signs that contained a clear trial﴾ (44:33): Thus they were tested through these signs. When their examination and trial were complete, and the period of their caliphate and their preference over the nations of the world came to an end, then, because of their deviation and error, they were seized, other peoples were set over them, and they were repeatedly faced with exile, and abasement was decreed for them. It was said to them that whenever you exceed the limits and act with rebellion, you will be humiliated and disgraced. This condition will remain until the Day of Resurrection.

***

After the observations of the destructive journey of Pharaoh and his chiefs, in which Moses (peace be upon him) and his people were granted deliverance and they were tested through it, the discourse now turns again to the polytheists' belief in resurrection after death. These people doubted, and indeed denied, being raised after death. This subject is taken up again from the angle that being raised after death is part of the true blueprint of this universe, because it is the truth, the universe itself exists upon the truth, and the demand of truth is that people be raised after death.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 44, verses 34–42:

Verses 34 to 42

The polytheists of Arabia used to say: "This is only our first death, and we shall not be raised again." By "the first" they meant that the warnings of resurrection and gathering that are recited to us are merely this first death. They said that this is death, and that everything ends with it, because their forefathers died only once and none of them ever returned to this world. Nobody was ever raised up again. Their demand was always: "If resurrection is true, then bring back our forefathers."

But on this matter they did not reflect on the wisdom of resurrection, nor did they perceive that resurrection and rising again are a stage of human development, with a specific wisdom and a defined purpose. That purpose is this: to see what each person did in the first stage of life. Those who are good, and who adopted good conduct in this stage of worldly life, should be given a good recompense, and those who adopted evil conduct here should be given its due. And they should be given a wretched and filthy life. If the good are not given their due reward and the wrongdoers are not given fitting punishment, this would not be just. The demand of this wisdom is that after the present stage of life has ended on this whole earth, there should be a resurrection and a reckoning. Therefore it is not possible that, on the demand of a few people, this whole scheme of the universe should be destroyed and a drama of resurrection staged for a few individuals or a single group, and their demand fulfilled, when they do not even believe in being raised after death, a matter of which all the messengers have unanimously given information. Reason also demands this when one reflects well on this life; and if one reflects on the system of creation of Allah, a person can believe in the establishment of the Hour.

Before calling them to reflect on the fundamental design of the whole universe, their minds and hearts are directed to a historical event whose occurrence was well known to them, namely the people of Tubba' and the kings of Himyar. This history was well known to the people of that time, so only a brief allusion is made to it, in order that the fear of God's seizure be freshly renewed in their hearts.

﴿Are they better, or the people of Tubba' and those before them? We destroyed them because they were criminals.﴾ (44:37) In an atmosphere of this reminder, with trembling hearts and with the concept of Allah's seizure before them, they are directed to consider what the design of the creation of this whole universe is. Within this universe a truth of great depth has been placed with deliberate purpose, and its demand is that resurrection and gathering are inevitable.

﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play. We did not create them except with truth, but most of them do not know. Indeed, the Day of Decision is the appointed time for all of them, the Day when no close friend will avail another close friend in anything, nor will they be helped, except those on whom Allah has mercy. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.﴾ (44:38–42) This is a most subtle indication that there is a delicate connection between the heavens and the earth and the creatures created between them, and the matter of resurrection and gathering, and that human nature can perceive this connection when it reflects deeply on the creation of this universe.

The fact is that the design and scheme of the creation of this universe are based on an extremely intricate and profound technology. All its subtleties are arranged with a purpose and a will. This creation is highly coordinated, and in it everything is according to a measure suited to its purpose; there is neither decrease nor increase. Everything fits perfectly within its environment. If one considers the form in which each thing has been created, it appears that it is necessary in this way, and it is far from possible that such an intricate technology came into being by mere chance, within this whole universe, which is terrifyingly vast.

The truth is that reflecting well on all these matters shows that this universe too has a great purpose, and that it can be fulfilled only if resurrection and gathering are accepted. This universe is established upon truth; nothing in it is false. Its end is something that has not yet occurred. This end and purpose are not fulfilled by death alone, because death is the end of this world, the conclusion of this short journey of the world. Resurrection and gathering are necessary even on logical grounds, because when creation rests on truth, the judgment between good and evil must also rest on truth. From the beginning of life, man has been given the capacity for righteousness and corruption, and here he chooses either righteousness or corruption; therefore he should receive the reward of righteousness and the punishment of corruption.

That man has been given the capacity for good and evil, and that Allah did not create man in vain, means that the end of good and evil is necessary, and this end must come after the short life of this world. Therefore resurrection and gathering are present within the design of the creation of this universe. This is why, after saying that the universe was not created in vain, the mention of the Hour comes.

﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision is the appointed time for all of them, the Day when no close friend will avail another close friend in anything, nor will they be helped, except those on whom Allah has mercy. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.﴾ (44:40–42)

This matter of the Hour is brought here in a highly coherent way, connected with what came before it in the verses. The demand of wisdom and truth is that there be a Day of Decision, on which judgments are settled among people, and the decisions of guidance and misguidance are made, goodness is honoured, and evil and wickedness are punished, and people are free from all earthly supports; there is no refuge for kin and relatives there. They go there alone, just as the Creator brought them into being. The Creator there gives them the recompense for what they earned. No one helps them, no one shows them mercy, and there is only the trust in and the grace of Allah, the Absolute Master, the Mighty, the Merciful. For it is He who brought them onto this earth and set them to work, and it is He who will punish them. And the brief life between their settling here and their being raised up is a life of trial and testing.

Thus Allah shows that truth is deposited in the original design of the creation of this universe and in the structure of the heavens and the earth, and it is clearly evident that the creation of this universe has a purpose.

*****

After these matters, now one of the scenes of the Hereafter: the punishment of the rebellious and the reward for the obedient. This is a most frightful and intense scene, and it harmonises with the atmosphere of this entire surah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 44, verse 43–57:

Verses 43 to 57

This scene begins with the presentation of the tree of Zaqqum, which will be the food of the wicked. It will be as bitter as the dregs of oil are bitter. This is a frightening portrayal of the food of the people of Hell, and this sediment will boil in the belly just as water boils in a cauldron. In the bellies of these wicked people, who displayed arrogance towards their Lord and towards His Messenger ﷺ, the trustworthy one, the command of God is issued thus against these "nobles":

﴿Seize him and drag him into the midst of the Blazing Fire. Then pour over his head the torment of boiling water.﴾ (44:47–48) "Seize him and drag him roughly into the midst of Hell, and pour over his head the torment of scalding water." That is: seize him with utmost harshness. Bind him tightly and then drag him, pushing and shoving, towards Hell; there should be no gentleness and no respectful arrest. And pour over their heads water so scalding that it cooks them. With this harshness, pulling, pushing, dragging, burning with hot water and branding, cast them into the interior of Hell, and then also say:

﴿Taste it! Indeed, you were the mighty, the noble.﴾ (44:49) "Taste it! Surely you were the mighty and the honourable one." Those who claim to be mighty and noble without true honour and nobility will receive a punishment like this. This is what you used to do against Allah and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. This conclusion corresponds to its beginning and to the line of argument adopted in it. The beginning was with the mention of the Book, the revelation of the Book, and its purpose of revelation, namely warning and admonition.
